items.why: The report says "A1g stiffens and E2g1 softens with thickness" and lists separations that grow from 19.23 (B) to 25.06 (C).
It assigns "B = 1L (19.23 ± 0.11 cm-1), A = 2L (21.45 ± 0.08)" and says the separation "separates B, A and the thick pair cleanly".

It gives "D = about 4L (24.26 ± 0.03, moderate confidence, ≥4L), C = bulk-like (25.06 ± 0.07)", notes "The separation saturates above about 4 to 5L", and says D and C "are not resolved from each other beyond 'at least 4L'".

It warns that "Absolute intensity is not layer number. Interference on 285 nm SiO2 modulates it", but it does not describe the rise to about 4L and then the fall, and it treats Si-normalised intensity as a "monotonic" trend supporting B < A < D ≲ C.

It states "Strain or doping can shift A1g/E2g1 by 1 to 2 cm-1 and so mimic one layer difference" and cites strain softening E' and doping softening and broadening A1g, but it gives no strain coefficient.
It reports the A1g FWHM as broadest in A (6.2 to 6.4, "as expected for 2L") and narrowest in C (2.9), with "E2g1 FWHM is the same in all four (2.04 to 2.18)".
It checks the Si line ("all four spectra sit about 0.7 cm-1 low against Si") and asks "Was the spectrometer calibrated (Si at 520.7?) before each measurement?"

wrong_claims.why: Layer numbers come from the mode separation, and intensity is used only as supporting evidence ("Absolute intensity is not layer number").
It states the correct trend: E2g1 softens and the separation grows with thickness.
It calls the feature a "Cosmic-ray spike in C... removed at 265.1 cm-1 (one to two pixels)", not a Raman band.
